q: 1. For construction of structures under water, the type of lime used, is .............
explain: Hydraulic lime contains silica and alumina, which allow it to set and harden under water by chemical reaction (hydration) rather than by carbonation from the air.

q: 2. Pozzolana (or surkhi) is used in lime .............
options: to decrease the cost of construction
explain: Pozzolana reacts with the calcium hydroxide in lime to form compounds with cementitious properties, effectively imparting hydraulic properties to non-hydraulic lime.

q: 3. The type of steel used for precision leveling staff, is .............
explain: Invar is an alloy of steel and nickel with a very low coefficient of thermal expansion, ensuring that the precision of the leveling staff is not affected by temperature changes.

q: 4. For the manufacture of stainless steel, steel is mixed with .............
explain: Chromium is the essential alloying element in stainless steel, providing the corrosion resistance by forming a passive oxide layer.

q: 5. The cement mortar mix commonly used for external plastering and plastering of reinforced cement concrete works is .............
explain: A richer mix of 1:3 (cement:sand) is used for external plastering to ensure high durability and resistance to moisture penetration.

q: 6. The process of applying cement mortar under pressure through a nozzle is called .............
explain: Guniting is a process where a dry mixture of cement and sand is shot through a nozzle using compressed air, with water added at the nozzle.

q: 7. Slump test facilitates .............
options: controlling of water-cement ratio of concrete during construction
the determination of initial and final setting times of cement
the determination of workability of concrete
explain: As Per Book Key A. The slump test is a simple field test used to measure the consistency or workability of a fresh concrete mix.

q: 8. Slacking of lime is affected by ............
explain: Slaking is the chemical process of adding water to quicklime (CaO), which converts it into hydrated lime [Ca(OH)2] with the evolution of heat.

q: 9. The coefficient of linear expansion of concrete is ............
options: almost same as that of steel
many times more than that of steel
explain: Concrete and steel have very similar thermal expansion coefficients ($12 	imes 10^{-6}/°C$), which prevents structural failure during temperature changes in Reinforced Cement Concrete.

q: 11. The lime which consists almost entirely of calcium oxide, is called ............
explain: Rich lime (or Fat lime) contains over 95% CaO. It slakes vigorously and is used for finishing work like white-washing.

q: 12. The lime which contains more than 30% of clayey impurities in the form of silica, alumina and iron oxide, is known as ............
explain: Poor or Lean lime has high impurity levels (over 30%). It slakes slowly and makes poor mortar, used only for low-grade work.

q: 13. Eminently hydraulic lime is one in which the percentage of silica, alumina and iron oxide is ......
explain: Eminently hydraulic lime contains 25-30% clayey impurities, allowing it to set under water in 1-2 days.

q: 14. The hydraulic lime which resembles very much with Portland cement in its chemical composition is called ............
explain: Because of its high silicate content, eminently hydraulic lime has properties similar to cement, especially its ability to set without air.

q: 15. Poor or lean lime ............
options: slakes rapidly with considerable evolution of heat
takes very long time to develop adequate strength
explain: As per Key D but As per google Lean lime has slow slaking and setting times and develops strength much more slowly than fat or hydraulic lime.

q: 16. The commonly used lime for works under water or in damp situation is ............
explain: Eminently hydraulic lime is used for underwater structures because it hardens through chemical reaction with water, not air.

q: 17. The process of adding the required quantity of water to quick lime in order to convert it in hydrated lime, is known as ............
explain: Slaking is the controlled hydration of CaO to form Ca(OH)2. If water is added to a large mass, it is often called slaking.

q: 18. The advantage of adding pozzolana (or surkhi) to lime is to ............
explain: Pozzolanas react with lime to improve the hydraulic properties, reduce shrinkage, and increase the overall durability of the mortar.

q: 19. The commonly used lime in white washing is ............
explain: Fat lime is preferred for white-washing because it has a high degree of whiteness and good plasticity.

q: 20. The lime mortar is made from ............
explain: For structural masonry, hydraulic lime is preferred over fat lime because it provides better strength and weather resistance.

q: 21. Quick lime on reaction with water gives ............
explain: The product of the slaking process (CaO + H2O) is calcium hydroxide, commonly known as slaked lime.

q: 22. The constituent in lime which retard the slaking action and increase the rapidity of setting, is ...
explain: The constituent in lime which retards the slaking action and increases the rapidity of setting is silica.

q: 23. The main constituent of a Portland cement is ............
explain: Lime (CaO) is the most significant component of cement (60-67%). Deficient lime reduces strength, while excess lime makes it unsound.

q: 24. The calcinations of pure lime result in ............
explain: The calcination of pure limestone (calcium carbonate) at high temperatures, typically above , removes carbon dioxide and results in the production of quick lime, also known as caustic lime or burnt lime

q: 25. The silicious and aluminous minerals, which do not have cementitious qualities by themselves but which react with lime in the presence of water to form cementitious compounds, are known as ............
explain: Pozzolanas (like fly ash or surkhi) react with the byproduct of lime/cement hydration to create stable, glue-like binders.

q: 26. If a timber is having three annual rings, it's age is about ............
explain: In exogenous trees, one annual ring generally represents one year of growth.

q: 27. The time required for air seasoning of soft wood is ............
explain: Air seasoning of softwoods typically takes about 2 to 3 months (60 to 90 days) depending on the climate and thickness of the timber.

q: 28. Which of the following timbers is suitable for making sports goods?
explain: Mulberry is flexible and tough, making it the ideal choice for hockey sticks, tennis rackets, and cricket bats.

q: 29. The disease of dry rot in timber is caused by ............
explain: Dry rot is a fungal decay caused by certain fungi that thrive in damp, unventilated conditions where they convert wood into dry, powdery mass.

q: 30. Creosote oil is derived from ............
explain: Creosote is a preservative for timber obtained through the distillation of coal tar or wood tar.

q: 31. The limit of proportionality is applicable more in the case of ............
explain: Mild steel follows Hooke's Law very strictly up to its limit of proportionality, showing a clearly defined linear relationship between stress and strain.

q: 32. The ingredient which accounts for the most in cement is ............
explain: Lime (Calcium Oxide) constitutes about 60% to 67% of Portland cement.

q: 33. The ingredient which accounts for the least in cement is ............
explain: Among the major ingredients (Lime, Silica, Alumina, Iron Oxide), Iron Oxide is typically present in the smallest quantity (about 0.5% to 6%).

q: 34. The timber having maximum resistance against white ants, is obtained from ............
explain: As Per key B But As Per Indiabix and zonetech D is correct answer cause Teak contains natural oils that make it highly resistant to white ants (termites) and insects.

q: 35. The variety of pig iron used for manufacture of wrought iron, is ............
explain: White forge pig iron is typically used for the production of wrought iron through the puddling process.

q: 36. For light and ornamental casting, the most unsuitable pig iron, is ............
explain: As per key D is correct but as per google baba White pig iron is brittle and hard to cast into delicate shapes; Grey pig iron is much more suitable for fine castings.

q: 37. According to I.S. 399 - 1963, the weight of the timber is specified at ............
explain: Standard weight specifications for timber are measured at a 12% moisture content level, which represents seasoned wood.

q: 38. The maximum quantity of calcium chloride used as an accelerator in cement in percentage by weight of cement is ............
explain: Calcium chloride is used to speed up setting, but it is generally restricted to 2% by weight because higher amounts can lead to corrosion of steel reinforcement.

q: 39. The rocks which are formed due to cooling of magma at considerable depth from earth's surface are called ............
explain: Plutonic rocks (like granite) form deep within the crust where slow cooling leads to large mineral crystals.

q: 40. The rocks which are formed due to cooling of magma at a relatively shallow depth from the earth surface are called ............
explain: Hypabyssal rocks (like dolerite) form at shallow depths, showing crystal sizes intermediate between plutonic and volcanic rocks.

q: 41. The aggregate is called fine aggregate if it is completely retained on ............
explain: Fine aggregate passes through a 4.75 mm sieve and is mostly retained on a 0.15 mm (150-micron) sieve..

q: 42. The aggregate is called coarse aggregate if it is completely retained on ............
explain: According to IS standards, aggregates that are retained on a 4.75 mm sieve are classified as coarse aggregate, while those passing through are fine aggregate.

q: 43. The bulking of sand is due to ............
options: the increase in space between the particles caused by the surface tension effect of moisture
the swelling of air in voids
explain: Bulking of sand occurs when moisture forms a thin film around sand particles, and surface tension pushes the particles apart, increasing the overall volume.

q: 44. The cement mortar mix generally used for masonry work is ............
explain: A 1:6 ratio (1 part cement to 6 parts sand) is the standard mix for general brickwork and masonry construction.

q: 45. The cement mortar mix generally used for internal plastering is ............
explain: As per Key of book For internal plastering on brick walls, a 1:5 mortar mix is typically recommended for a balance of workability and strength.

q: 46. Wrought iron is manufactured from pig iron by ............
explain: The process involves refining the pig iron, followed by puddling to remove impurities, and shingling to squeeze out slag.

q: 47. Brittleness of cold is due to an excess of ............
explain: Excess phosphorus in steel or iron causes 'cold shortness,' making the metal brittle and liable to crack when cold worked.

q: 48. Red short iron cracks when bent due to the presence of ............
explain: Excess sulphur causes 'red shortness' or 'hot shortness,' meaning the iron becomes brittle and cracks at high temperatures (red heat).

q: 49. The process of decarbonising pig iron completely and then adding proper percentage of carbon for manufacturing steel is called ............
explain: As per Key A is Answer but as per google In the Bessemer process, air is blown through molten pig iron to oxidize impurities and carbon; then, a specific amount of carbon/manganese is added back.

q: 50. Dolomite is a lime stone which contains carbonate of magnesia upto ............
explain: Dolomite is a sedimentary rock containing a high percentage of magnesium carbonate, often reaching up to 45%.
